clue.text: Dessert produced by French chef, guy with good English

parts.note: Raymond Blanc is a famous French chef working in Britain
a guy is a man

explanation.surface: A pudding made by a French chef together with a well-behaved Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: Raymond Blanc is a celebrated French chef with restaurants in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A milky, set pudding is a classic example of a dessert.

clue.text: Smart of one on a diet to lose pounds

definitions.note: verb: to smart is to feel stung or resentful

indicators.note: to lose says a letter is dropped from the dieter's word

parts.note: someone dieting to shed weight is a slimmer
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling (libra)

explanation.surface: Chic style of someone dieting in order to shed weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' looks like an adjective about style, but it is a verb: to smart is to burn with resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe quietly with anger is close to stinging or rankling with resentment.

clue.text: Intimate conversation between retired couple?

parts.note: retired here means gone to bed, not stopped working, so the couple chat with heads on cushions

explanation.surface: A cosy chat between an elderly pensioner pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' suggests pensioners; here it means having retired for the night, so the chat happens in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names private, affectionate chat between lovers lying in bed.

clue.text: Begrudge diplomat lacking nothing

indicators.note: lacking says a piece must be taken out of the diplomat's word

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomat sent on a mission
O, the round zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Resenting an ambassador who has nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel jealous resentment of someone's good fortune is to begrudge it.

clue.text: Instruments used to fix Oscar's crowns

indicators.note: used to fix says the brass instruments hold the letter fixed in place inside them

parts.note: cornets are brass instruments
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Tools employed to repair the crowns belonging to someone called Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar is the radio code word for the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Small crowns worn by nobles are coronets, so the plural fits crowns.

clue.text: Reproduced in black and another colour

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
red is another colour besides black

explanation.surface: Something printed again in black and a second colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reproduced' suggests copying; here it means having produced offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that have produced young have bred, the past tense of breed.

clue.text: One acting as monarch, for example, in musical

indicators.note: in says the example abbreviation sits within the show's name

parts.note: Rent is a Broadway musical by Jonathan Larson
EG is short for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: An actor playing a king, for instance, in a stage musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who rules while the true monarch is a child or absent is a regent.

clue.text: Cornelius is cool changing route that would lead to conflict

definitions.text: route that would lead to conflict

indicators.note: changing says the letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Cornelius coolly alters a route heading for trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges CORNELIUS IS COOL into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A path that will end in a crash is a figurative heading towards confrontation or clash.

clue.text: Garments husband put in closet, surprisingly

indicators.note: put in says the husband's letter is placed inside the shuffled letters
surprisingly says the letters of closet turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A husband has unexpectedly stored garments in the closet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges CLOSET into CLOTES, and 'put in' places H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments are items of dress, the things we wear.

clue.text: Admit being depressed losing diamonds

indicators.note: losing says a letter is dropped from the gloomy word

parts.note: feeling down is feeling depressed
D is the abbreviation for the card suit diamonds

explanation.surface: Confessing to being low after losing one's jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up to something is to admit it.

clue.text: Pamper little Mary old theologian left in church

parts.note: Molly is a pet form of the name Mary

indicators.note: in says the three short pieces go inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
DD is a Doctor of Divinity

explanation.surface: Spoiling a young Mary while an old cleric is left behind in church.
explanation.walkthrough: CE (Church of England) holds O, DD (Doctor of Divinity) and L.
explanation.definitionFit: To pamper is to treat someone with excessive indulgence and coddling care.

clue.text: Greek poet in river

parts.note: someone in is at home

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek poet found inside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but gives HOME, as in 'staying in'.
explanation.definitionFit: The supposed author of the Iliad and Odyssey is the archetypal ancient Greek epic poet.

clue.text: Comic due at show cancelled because of rain

indicators.note: comic says the letters of the next three words are treated in a funny, jumbled way

explanation.surface: A comedian's scheduled performance is rained off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic' looks like a person but rearranges DUE AT SHOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporting event abandoned through a downpour is said to be rained off in that idiom.

clue.text: Season swell deep-fried pancake

parts.note: spring is a season of the year
the sea's swell is a roll of waves

explanation.surface: A seasoned, swelling fried pancake.
explanation.definitionFit: This Chinese starter is a thin pancake wrapper filled and deep-fried.

clue.text: Exposed, landlord in communication intended for publication

parts.note: exposed means open, uncovered
a landlord lets property, so is a letter

explanation.surface: A landlord is publicly exposed in a published letter.
explanation.walkthrough: A landlord is one who lets, hence a 'letter'.
explanation.definitionFit: A public message addressed to someone but printed in a newspaper is this kind of missive.

clue.text: Famous singer posed to accommodate popular artist

indicators.note: to accommodate says the posing word makes room for another piece inside it

parts.note: a model who posed for a portrait sat
in means popular, fashionable
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A celebrity vocalist sat for a portrait to oblige a well-known painter.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a crossword stock artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank, the crooner of My Way, is one of the most famous vocalists of the last century.

clue.text: Tavener's first work — score is superb

indicators.note: first says only the opening letter of the composer's name is used

parts.note: OP is opus, a musical work
to score is to cut a notch

explanation.surface: The composer John Tavener's debut piece has a superb musical score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' looks musical but means a notch, a cut mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of the very highest quality is excellent or superb.

clue.text: Admire characters in wire spectacles

indicators.note: characters in says the letters sit within the words wire spectacles

explanation.surface: Admiring a pair of wire-framed glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone in esteem or high regard is to admire them.

clue.text: Renting in extremely tolerable French city

indicators.note: extremely says only the outermost letters of tolerable are kept

parts.note: Nancy is a city in north-east France

explanation.surface: Finding a rental in a fairly acceptable French city.
explanation.definitionFit: Occupying a property as a tenant, paying rent, is holding a lease.

clue.text: Hips and knees loose type of coat revealed

indicators.note: loose says the letters of the two body parts are set free and rearranged

explanation.surface: Hips and knees are on show, presumably beneath a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat made from a fleece-lined hide is a well-known type of warm coat.

clue.text: Seafood affected one after start of show

indicators.note: start of says only the first letter of show is used

parts.note: camp means affected, exaggerated in manner
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone affected by seafood after the start of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: The order is S, then CAMP, then I; 'after' signals CAMP and I follow S.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaded langoustine tails are a familiar seafood dish.

clue.text: Pony frisking around close to bell tower

indicators.note: around says the jumbled letters surround a further letter
frisking says the pony's letters skip about into a new order
close to says only the final letter of bell is used

explanation.surface: A pony capering about near a bell tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frisking' turns PONY into PYON, which goes 'around' L.
explanation.definitionFit: A pylon is a tall steel tower carrying power lines.

clue.text: Currency unit once used in Guadeloupe set aside

indicators.note: used in says the letters are found within the run Guadeloupe set aside

explanation.surface: A former currency used in Guadeloupe has been put aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain's monetary unit before the euro is a former currency unit.

clue.text: A problem the angler may have?

definitions.meaning: a messy complicated problem, best left unopened
a tin of bait an angler might carry

explanation.surface: An angler's trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a tangle of troubles; literally, a tin of bait for fishing.

clue.text: A leading orchestra, as well

parts.note: LSO, the London Symphony Orchestra, is a leading orchestra

explanation.surface: A top orchestra, as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and as well are plain synonyms meaning in addition.

clue.text: Extra papers that you and I must hold

indicators.note: must hold says the pronoun goes around the documents

parts.note: you and I together are we
ID is identity papers

explanation.surface: Additional documents that the two of us must keep.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a wide is a ball out of the batter's reach, giving the batting side an extra run.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket this is one kind of extra, a run not scored off the bat.

clue.text: Money fool rejected

indicators.note: rejected says the word for a fool is turned back

parts.note: a nit is a fool, a nitwit

explanation.surface: A fool turned down cash.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Old British slang for cash, as in tin in the pocket.

clue.text: Countrywide issue, to-do — copy letters sent out

indicators.note: sent out says the letters of to-do and copy letters are dispatched into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A national fuss as copies of letters are posted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent out' rearranges TO-DO COPY LETTERS. The phrase means services varying by postal area, a British complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes unequal public services depending on where you live, a nationwide grievance.
